t: Minimum Adjacent Swaps for K Consecutive Ones: Median Gathering on Compressed Positions
o:
## Understanding the problem

Only adjacent swaps are allowed, and each swap slides a 1 across one 0. We must gather some k of the existing ones into one contiguous run as cheaply as possible. Adjacent swaps never reorder the ones, so the chosen k ones occupy k consecutive seats **in their original order** — the total cost equals how far the group travels.

Compress first: nums = [1,0,0,1,0,1] has ones at pos = [0,3,5]. Substitute b[j] = pos[j] - j (here [0,2,3]): gathering window i..i+k-1 onto consecutive targets anchored at m costs exactly sum of |b[j] - m|.

**Examples:** Example 1 — windows of k = 2 over [0,2,3]: pair (2,3) anchors anywhere in [2,3] for cost 1. Example 2 — b = [0,5,5], all three anchor at median 5, cost 5. Example 3 — ones already adjacent, so a zero-cost window exists.

With n up to 1e5 we need near-linear time, and totals reach ~1e10, demanding 64-bit arithmetic.
k: Adjacent swaps preserve the order of the 1s, so gathering equals sliding the chosen ones onto consecutive targets in order.
The shift b_j = pos_j - j collapses all targets to a single anchor: cost = sum |b_j - anchor|, minimized at the median.
A sliding window of size k over b with prefix sums evaluates every candidate group in O(1).

a.n: Approach 1: Brute-Force Window Cost via Median
a.i: Record positions of all ones, convert to b[j] = pos[j] - j, then examine every window of k consecutive ones. For each window take its median (any point between the two central values works for even k) and sum absolute deviations — exactly the minimal swap count for that group. Clear and correct, but each window costs O(k), too slow for the largest inputs.
s: Extract pos = indices of 1s; set b[j] = pos[j] - j.
For each window start i, let m = b[i + k/2] (upper median).
Window cost = sum of |b[j] - m| over j in the window.
Return the minimum cost across all windows.
a.t: O(C * k) — C windows (C = number of ones), each summed naively

a.n: Approach 2: Prefix Sums + Sliding Window over Transformed Positions
a.i: Keep the b transformation but evaluate each window in O(1). Splitting at the upper median mid, the cost is (left half pulled up to b[mid]) plus (right half pulled down to b[mid]); each half is a count-times-anchor-minus-range-sum expressible through one prefix-sum array. Sweep all windows once.
s: Build b[j] = pos[j] - j and its prefix sums pre.
For window start i, set mid = i + k/2 and m = b[mid].
Right cost = (pre[i+k] - pre[mid+1]) - m * (i + k - 1 - mid).
Answer = min over all i of left + right.
a.t: O(n + C) — one pass to compress positions plus C constant-time window evaluations
a.sp: O(C) — the b array and its prefix sums

w:
## Wrap-up

Present the compression-plus-median argument — it is the heart of the problem — then implement the prefix-sum sliding window. Keep the brute-force scan only as a small-case sanity check.

Common pitfalls:

- Skipping the b_j = pos_j - j shift: anchoring targets at raw positions forces per-element offsets and off-by-one bugs.
- Even-k medians: any value between the two central b entries is optimal; the upper median keeps the split clean.
- 32-bit overflow — distances reach about 1e10, so accumulate in 64-bit everywhere.
- Misreading the goal: gather exactly k ones (not all), and remember ones cannot pass through each other.

Follow-ups: force the block to land at a specific position, maximize the longest run within a move budget (binary search on k reusing this solution), or extend to circular arrangements.
